Part 1:

This Indian Standard ( Part 10 ), which is identical with IS0 5834/1-l 985 `Implants for by the surgery .- Ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene - Part 1 : Powder form' issued International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ), was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendations of the Orthopaedic Instruments and Accessories Sectional Committee and approval of the Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Division Council. In the adopted standard, certain terminology and:conventions are not identical used in Indian Standards; attention is particularly drawn to the following: Comma ( , ) has been used as a decimal mark while in Indian is to use a point ( , ) as the decimal marker. Scope

and field

of application

3.2

This part of IS0 5834 specifies the requirements and corresponding test methods for moulding material in powder form made from ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) for use in the manufacture of surgical implants. It does not apply to finished products.

Definitions

6

Flow

properties

For the purpose of this part of IS0 8834, the following definitions apply. 3.1 flow vake (lBO/lO) : The tensile stress in newtons per square millimetre necessary to elongate the length of the web of the specimen in a suitable medium (for example glycerin) at 180 OC by 800 96 in 10 min when the test is in accordance with annex,A. This flow value is designated "F (150/10)"

For both Type A and Type B material, either the flow value F (150/10) determined in accordance with 8.1 and annex A, shall be not less than 0,2 N/mm?, or the relative solution viscosity determined in accordance with 8.2 and annex 6 shall be not fess than 1,95.
NOTE - Compliance with either of the above test requirements indicates satisfactory polymer molecular weight.

A.4 A.2 Principle

Test sample

Six test specimens are prepared from a compression moulded plate. The time taken to elongate the web of the test specimen 600 % at 150 OC is determined under various loads increasing from l?O to 300 gf from the first test to the sixth.

A representative sample sufficient for the tests to be carried out shall be taken from the moulding powder under test.

Annex Method for determining

B viscosity of UHMWPE

the relative solution moulding material
(This annex forms part of the standard.)

B.l

Scope

and field

of application

B.4.3

Xylene, chemical grade.

This annex specifies a method for determining the solution viscosity ratio of UHMWPE moulding material in powder form.

Cleaning solution : sulphuric acid-potassium B.4.4 dichromate mixture. B.4.5 8.4.6 Acetone. Source of dry nitrogen.

B.2

Principle

The moulding powder is dissolved in decalin to,05 g/100 ml) at 150 Y, and the viscosity of the solution measured at 135 OC using a Ubbelohde No. 1 viscometer. This viscosity is compared with the viscosity of the solvent itself determined under similar conditions.

8.5

Test

sample

A representative sample sufficient for the test to be carried out shall be taken from the moulding powder under test.

B.3

Apparatus
(a suitable apparatus is

8.3.1 Distillation apparatus described in ASTM D 16011. B.3.2 Viscometer, Ubbelohde kinetic energy correction. 8.3.3 B.3.4 B.3.5 0.1 ml. Vacuum drying oven.

B.5
B.6.1

Procedure
Decalin preparation

No. 1, having a known

Distil approximately 200 ml of decalin (8.4.1) in accordance with ASTM D 1601, and add 0,2 % of phenyl-P-naphthylamine 18.4.2). B.6.2 Cleaning the viscometer

Microscope

slide cover slip. Clean the viscometer (8.3.2) thoroughly with the dichromate cleaning solution (8.4.4). wash several times with distilled water, rinse with acetone (8.4.5) and purge with dry nitrogen (8.4.6). B.6.3 Preparation of solution in decalin

Burette, of capacity 100 ml, graduated in intervals of

B.3.6 Conical flask, of capacity 250 ml, fitted with a glass stopper. B.3.7 Vacuum aspirator.

B.3.8 Water bath, a constant temperature bath, capable of being controlled at 135 + 1 OC. 8.3.9 8.3.10 8.3.11 8.3.12 Hot plate with magnetic stirrer.

Glass funnel with heating mantle. Stopwatch, Analytical accurate to 0.2 s.

Dry the test sample of UHMWPE powder in the vacuum oven 18.3.3) for 2 h at 60 OC. Weigh a test portion of the dried powder amounting to 35 to 43 mg on to the slide cover slip (8.3.4). Using the burette 18.3.51, transfer the decalin at room temperature into the conical flask 18.3.61, the transferred volume in millilitres being equal to 1.8 times the mass of test portion in milligrams; for example for a 36 mg test portion of UHMWPE, 64.8 ml of decalin ir measured into the flask. Heat the decalin, while stirring, to 150 OC. Then drop into the flask the test portion of UHMWPE and its slide cover slip. Continue stirring at 150 OC for 1 h. B.6.4 Determination of viscosity

balance. Place the cleaned viscometer in the constant temperature bath (8.3.81, fill with decalin, and allow it to come to thermal equilibrium at 135 f 1 OC. Determine the flow time of the solvent. Remove the decalin with the vacuum aspirator (8.3.7) and wash the viscometer with 200 ml of warm (110 to 120 "Cl xylene (8.4.31. Remove with suction and aspirate with dry air or nitrogen to dry the viscometer (2 or 3 mini. Ensure that the whole viscometer is dry.
